reason: E1 shows that local lattice distortion and heterogeneous strain landscapes arise from frustrated crystallization in HEAs, supporting the premise of heterogeneous interfacial structure. E2 and E3 describe dislocation-mediated plasticity and twinning in bulk HEAs, but neither addresses interfaces, sustained creep loading, or the specific claim that interfacial heterogeneities govern progressive plastic deformation under creep. The cited evidence therefore provides only partial, indirect support for the key premises.
premises: Interfaces in HEA multilayers exhibit heterogeneous short-range chemical order and lattice distortions
These interfacial heterogeneities create amplified local stress concentrations under sustained load
Enhanced local stresses at interfaces promote dislocation nucleation and motion
Limited nano-twinning can accommodate dislocation activity at interfaces
This interface-mediated plasticity produces spatially heterogeneous strain, unlike conventional multilayers
